source_span: There's very little in the Muse offering to suggest it disrupts the unit economics of the banking system... So this feels macro and systematic led to me, with that systematic flow catalyzing de-risking out of fundamental investors.
source_chain: Muse doesn't disrupt bank unit economics, therefore the selling in consensus names (C/MS/GS/USB) versus regional outperformance is a positioning unwind by systematic flow, not a fundamental re-rating, therefore O'Dwyer fades the move, favoring MS/PNC/FITB; invalidated if the AI capex build turns out to be a funding headwind for banks rather than the opportunity he currently reads it as.
pulse_chain: JPMorgan's O'Dwyer says there is very little in what Muse does to disrupt bank unit economics, therefore the selling in consensus names (Citi/MS/GS/USB) against regional outperformance is a positioning unwind not a re-rating, therefore he fades it, sizing patiently and favoring MS/PNC/FITB. Goldman's financials desk instead reads the broader selloff as an uncertainty discount with a complete buyers' strike and no sector defense, therefore its own AI-selloff precedent says patience beats defending day one, resolved by product catalysts (Meta Connect, OpenAI Dev Day, Micron earnings) rather than valuation.
why: The pulse reproduces O'Dwyer's exact mechanism (Muse doesn't touch bank unit economics -> positioning unwind not re-rating -> fade toward MS/PNC/FITB) with correct attribution to JPMorgan, and layers in Goldman's contrasting uncertainty-discount read plus the Consumer Inertia basket mechanism (agents compress pricing power/retention/lifetime value in telecom/insurance/utilities/subscriptions) verbatim from the GS notes, without reversing any step, misattributing a bank, or swapping the invalidation/catalysts.
